what_works: India-centric rankings and geopolitical comparisons (e.g., 'India's Highest-Earning Cities' at 3,516 views, 'Top 5 Powerful Countries / India rank' at 3,316 views).
Bizarre, high-curiosity historical conflict narratives (e.g., 'Mystery of the 1962 War' at 2,617 views, 'The War Fought Over One Pig' at 116.6 views/day).
Hindi/Hinglish curiosity framing with emotional triggers and flag emojis ('🇮🇳', '😱', '🔥').
Durations kept tight between 29 and 51 seconds; shorter videos under 35s on dramatic topics ('1962 War' at 29s, 'Maritime Boundary' at 32s) perform consistently well above the 1,248 median.

diagnosis.hook: Underperforming videos fail at the first frame. They rely on explanatory textbook premises ('Photosynthesis Explained', 'The Incredible Power...') instead of shocking pattern interrupts, counter-intuitive claims, or urgent questions.
diagnosis.buildup: Low performers tend to deliver flat informational summaries rather than escalating tension. High-performing geopolitical shorts maintain momentum by holding the most controversial answer (e.g., India's rank, secret boundary fact) until the final third.
diagnosis.visuals: Flopped videos consistently lack custom thumbnails or distinctive visual anchors in the opening 2 seconds. Successful shorts show maps, flags, recognizable figures (Kim Jong Un, Taj Mahal), or high-contrast graphics instantly.
diagnosis.titles_topics: TruFact has a clear split: geopolitical/patriotic/bizarre history performs well (1,500 - 3,500 views), while school-level science, abstract biology, and niche foreign architecture completely tank (<100 views). Glitched titles like '...Empire 🚀Description:' destroy credibility.
diagnosis.other: Inconsistent language strategy. TruFact's audience responds significantly better to Hindi or Hinglish framing; purely formal English titles for biology/ancient history drop viewer engagement to near zero.

hook_rules: State a counter-intuitive paradox in the first 2 seconds (e.g., 'Duniya ka sabse mehenga pathar concrete se banta hai?').
Never start with greetings, self-introductions, or topic labels like 'Aaj hum baat karenge...'.
Introduce a visual disruption within frame 1 (split comparison, dynamic map zoom, or high-contrast text overlay).
Pose an open loop with high national or personal relevance (e.g., 'Bharat ka wo shehar jahan har teesra aadmi crorepati hai').
Keep the spoken hook under 12 words and deliver it at an energetic, brisk cadence.
buildup_rules: Use micro-reveals every 7-10 seconds to constantly reset the viewer's attention span.
Delay the payoff of the title's core question until the last 5-7 seconds of the video.
Escalate stakes using comparative metrics ('Lekin twist yahan nahi hai...', 'Isse bhi azeeb baat ye hui...').
Design a seamless loop by making the final sentence naturally lead back into the opening hook.
visual_rules: Change on-screen visual elements or camera angles every 1.5 to 2.5 seconds.
Use bold, 2-to-3 word kinetic captions highlighted in contrasting yellow and red rather than long text paragraphs.
Feature recognizable visual anchors (maps, flags, faces with extreme expressions, money/weapons) within the top 60% of the vertical frame.
Eliminate still images without motion; apply continuous slow zoom-ins, directional pans, or particle overlays.
title_rules: Keep titles under 60 characters so the core mystery is fully visible on mobile feeds without truncation.
Incorporate 1-2 high-impact emojis (🇮🇳, 😱, ⚔️, 💰) aligned with the emotional tone of the video.
Use Hinglish or Hindi script with curiosity words ('Kyun', 'Sachai', 'Galti', 'Secret').
Proofread every title thoroughly to prevent copy-paste artifacts like 'Description:' or redundant tags.
topic_rules: Double down on Indian geopolitics, military defense, untold border history, and wealth/city comparisons.
If covering global history, frame it through absurd or bizarre conflict lenses ('War fought over one pig') rather than dry dates.
Validate topic appeal: Ensure the subject triggers pride, disbelief, or intense curiosity before scripting.
avoid: Avoid school curriculum science topics (e.g., 'Photosynthesis Explained') with no narrative stakes.
Avoid generic wildlife biology facts unless tied to an extreme, unbelievable human interaction.
Avoid formal, academic English titles that read like encyclopedias or textbooks.
Avoid publishing with metadata errors, unformatted description scraps in titles, or missing visual thumbnails.
Avoid slow pacing or 50+ second runtimes on weak concepts; if the concept has only 20 seconds of substance, do not stretch it to 48 seconds.
